chunks: It is narrated from Abu Basir that he said:

When Dawood bin Ali had Mualla bin Khunais eliminated and had his body suspended in public view, it was a great tragedy for Imam Ja’far Sadiq (peace be upon him), which aggrieved him much. So he said to the killer: O Dawood, why have you got my friend and manager of the monetary affairs of my family, killed? By Allah, he is more honorable than you before Almighty Allah… It is a lengthy tradition.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja’far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمَعْلَى: Al-Ma'la, a title or part of the name Mualla bin Khunais
key_terms.خُنَيْس: Khunais, part of the name Mualla bin Khunais
key_terms.دَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Dawood bin Ali, the killer mentioned in the narration
key_terms.فَصَلَبَهُ: And he suspended him (crucified/hung his body)

ai.seo_question: What was Imam al-Sadiq's reaction to the killing of Mualla bin Khunais?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the emotional* underscores the high status of the *Muwakkil* (approved emissary) within the Shia tradition, illustrating that their martyrdom carries a unique spiritual weight that even the Imam acknowledges as superior to the killer's status. The Imam’s rhetorical question, 'On what basis did you kill my master and my support?', emphasizes the personal and theological bond between the Imam and his agents, framing their death not merely as a political loss but as a significant cosmic event. This incident serves as a key proof for the authority and reliability of the *Muwakkilat* system during the Minor Ghayba.
